data.text: The picture is consistent. Let me record the diagnosis.

data.reason: The firewall's WAN interface driver (vtnet0, VirtIO) hung — repeated "watchdog timeout on queue 0" with link flaps — so nothing can be transmitted on the WAN side even though addressing and routing are intact; the initial trigger was a cable-modem T3 ranging timeout at 02:01:44, but the modem has since rebooted and re-registered as OPERATIONAL while the stuck driver keeps the internet down.

data.cause: The firewall's WAN interface driver (vtnet0, VirtIO) hung — repeated "watchdog timeout on queue 0" with link flaps — so nothing can be transmitted on the WAN side even though addressing and routing are intact; the initial trigger was a cable-modem T3 ranging timeout at 02:01:44, but the modem has since rebooted and re-registered as OPERATIONAL while the stuck driver keeps the internet down.
evidence: dmesg -a shows repeated 'vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0' interleaved with 'link state changed to DOWN/UP' — the TX queue is hung and reloads only toggled the link without clearing it.

ping -c 3 -n 198.51.100.1 fails with 'ping: sendto: No buffer space available' (100% loss) — the kernel cannot push packets out vtnet0, yet netstat -m shows mbufs are not exhausted (0 denied), pointing at the NIC TX path, not memory.
arp -n shows the WAN gateway entry '? (198.51.100.1) at (incomplete) ... expired' — ARP never completes because frames never leave the hung interface.

netstat -i shows vtnet0 Oerrs=48211 and netstat -s confirms '48211 output packets dropped due to no bufs, etc.'; ifconfig still reports vtnet0 status active with lease 198.51.100.27, and netstat -rn shows the default route via 198.51.100.1 intact — so the lease/route themselves are fine.

/var/db/wan-watchdog/events.jsonl: outage_start 02:06, four wan reloads during this outage all rc=0 with no recovery, then a 03:30 decision of 'none' with reason 'reload_cap' (12 reloads in 24h) — repeated reconfiguration does not reset the hung driver.

/var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-events.jsonl: 'No Ranging Response received - T3 time-out' at 02:01:44, then 'Cable Modem Reboot ... registration complete' at 02:28:21; modem-metrics.jsonl shows uptime 5280s and status OPERATIONAL at 03:30 with healthy SNR (37.7 dB) — the modem recovered, so the remaining fault is on the firewall's NIC side.
data.recommendation: Reboot the firewall (gw.lan) to re-initialize the hung vtnet0 driver; another wan_reload will not help since four reloads already had no effect and the 24h reload cap is reached. The maintainer is away, so approve/perform the reboot via the available mechanism when possible (~4 minutes of network outage). A full interface/driver reset is what's needed, not a lease renewal.
data.detail: vtnet0 WAN NIC driver hung (watchdog timeouts on queue 0)
